interpretation: Structural validity and traceability do not establish completeness or learner readiness. Higher-level sources, alternate paths, and other source outcomes are inspection signals, not automatic defects. Do not delete edges or split decks without evaluating their contracts.

exclusions.subject: mathematics
exclusions.rationale: Specialized programs such as the Langlands correspondence, forcing research, higher categories and derived geometry are beyond this whole-field progression; their relevant algebraic, logical and geometric entry methods are included separately.

exclusions.subject: computer-science
exclusions.rationale: Vendor certifications and exhaustive platform-specific operations are excluded; programming, architecture, networking, security and distributed implementation methods are included.

exclusions.subject: computer-science
exclusions.rationale: Exhaustive frontier coverage of quantum computing, specialized programming-language metatheory and every AI architecture is not attempted; representative theory, verification and learning continuations are included.

exclusions.subject: biology
exclusions.rationale: Clinical licensure, veterinary practice and authorized human therapeutic procedures require separate professional programs; physiology, immunology, experimental ethics and biotechnology methods are included.

exclusions.subject: biology
exclusions.rationale: Exhaustive taxon-specific and disease-specific research catalogs are excluded; identification, evolutionary inference, organismal physiology and experimental methods are included.

exclusions.subject: chemistry
exclusions.rationale: Plant certification, pharmaceutical release authority and specialist chemical-engineering design are separate qualifications; chemical analysis, catalysis, material processing, mass balance and environmental decisions are included.

exclusions.subject: chemistry
exclusions.rationale: Exhaustive named-reaction catalogs and every frontier spectroscopy or synthesis platform are excluded; working synthesis, structural inference, dynamics and materials research routes are included.

exclusions.subject: physics
exclusions.domain: Additional frontier theories and engineering qualifications
exclusions.rationale: String theory, quantum gravity, exhaustive detector technologies and full reactor or accelerator engineering are beyond the proposal; relativity, field theory, plasma, nuclear and experimental foundations are included.

includes: Cloning and gene editing, reporter and imaging methods, perturbation screens, controls, causal validation and biotechnology research decisions.

outcomes.description: Design cloning and editing workflows, select delivery and confirmation assays and construct imaging and reporter measurements with specificity, off-target and expression controls.

Design arrayed or pooled screens with power, replication and batch controls, analyze effect estimates and false discoveries and validate candidate mechanisms through independent perturbation and rescue.

practice: Develop an approved low-risk editing or reporter study, or a full design with supplied data, including validation assays and a screened-hit follow-up plan.

includes: Animal tissues, neural and endocrine regulation, circulation, respiration, digestion, excretion, reproduction and comparative homeostasis.

outcomes.description: Explain interactions among major organ systems and infer regulatory changes from perturbation and time-course data across contrasting animal strategies.
Apply locally derived diffusion, pressure-flow, mass-balance and Nernst models to physiological transport, membrane potentials and negative feedback, stating equilibrium and steady-state limits.

practice: Analyze a dehydration, exercise or oxygen-limitation case using quantitative balances and competing feedback explanations.

includes: Cells, organismal organization, heredity, natural selection, major lineages and ecosystem relationships at an accessible descriptive level.

outcomes.description: Compare cellular and organismal organization, explain membranes and information-bearing molecules qualitatively, and distinguish observations from mechanistic claims.
Use simple inheritance examples and variation, reproduction and selection to explain population change without purposeful-evolution reasoning.
Read life-cycle, food-web and branching-tree diagrams and distinguish major microbial, fungal, plant and animal lineages.

practice: Build an evidence-annotated explanation of a biological phenomenon at cellular, organismal and population scales.

includes: Membranes, organelles, transport, cytoskeleton, cell cycle, replication, transcription, translation, signaling and perturbation-based inference.

outcomes.description: Infer cellular mechanisms from localization, time-course, inhibition and rescue data while distinguishing direct effects, feedback and alternative explanations.
Predict membrane transport, trafficking, cytoskeletal and cell-cycle behavior using molecular organization, concentration gradients and bounded binding models.
Represent DNA replication, transcription, RNA processing, translation and signaling, and predict effects of molecular changes on regulation and cellular state.

practice: Build and test competing explanations for a trafficking or gene-regulation phenotype using a supplied perturbation dataset.

includes: Conductance-based and integrate-and-fire neurons, neural networks, encoding models, spike likelihoods and model validation.

outcomes.description: Fit Poisson and point-process encoding models using taught discretized spike likelihoods and assess stimulus prediction, time-bin sensitivity, residual structure and causal interpretation limits.
Derive membrane current-balance equations, implement Hodgkin-Huxley and integrate-and-fire models and analyze recurrent-network equilibria and response dynamics.

practice: Implement a spiking model and fit an encoding model to recordings, comparing mechanistic plausibility with held-out predictive performance.

includes: Extinction risk, fragmentation, conservation genetics, restoration, ecosystem services, monitoring and management tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Assess population and habitat vulnerability using demographic, connectivity and genetic evidence; construct bounded population projections and evaluate restoration monitoring designs.
Compare management options using uncertain biological outcomes, costs, equity, local and Indigenous knowledge obligations and competing ecological objectives; justify adaptive decision rules.

practice: Prepare a conservation decision dossier with alternative actions, sensitivity analysis, stakeholder obligations and a measurable monitoring plan.

includes: Fertilization, axes, induction, morphogens, differentiation, morphogenesis, regeneration and developmental experiment design.

outcomes.description: Infer developmental mechanisms from fate mapping, transplantation, timed perturbation and rescue experiments and distinguish specification, determination and cell autonomy.
Represent lineage, positional information, gene-regulatory interactions and tissue mechanics to explain axis formation, differentiation and morphogenesis in contrasting organisms.

practice: Reconstruct a developmental regulatory model from lineage and perturbation evidence and propose a discriminating timed intervention.

includes: Population sampling, life tables, discrete growth, species interactions, diversity, food webs, nutrient cycling and disturbance.

outcomes.description: Calculate diversity and energy or nutrient budgets, interpret food webs and evaluate experiments on disturbance, succession and environmental change.
Estimate abundance and survival using quadrats, transects and capture-recapture assumptions; construct life tables and discrete population and interaction models.

practice: Design a field-sampling study and use its data or supplied records to estimate population state, quantify uncertainty and predict a disturbance response.

includes: Selection, drift, mutation, migration, mating systems, speciation, phylogenetic reasoning and comparative tests of adaptation.

outcomes.description: Calculate Hardy-Weinberg expectations and discrete-generation allele-frequency updates under selection, mutation and migration; distinguish deterministic change from drift.
Construct small character-based phylogenies, interpret common ancestry and speciation evidence and test adaptation claims against historical and nonadaptive alternatives.

practice: Analyze an allele-frequency time series and a comparative trait dataset, explicitly separating selection, demographic and ancestry explanations.

includes: Wright-Fisher models, coalescent genealogies, linkage, selection, demographic inference and model-based phylogenomics.

outcomes.description: Fit bounded demographic and phylogenetic likelihood models and distinguish selection, population structure, recombination and sequencing artifacts using simulations and model criticism.
Derive and simulate finite-population drift, mutation and selection models and elementary coalescent waiting times; calculate diversity, fixation and linkage summaries under stated assumptions.

practice: Infer population history from a bounded variant dataset and use simulated alternatives to test whether a selection interpretation is identifiable.

includes: Biological controls, sampling, randomization, microscopy, pipetting, dilution, aseptic handling, image measurement and research ethics.

outcomes.description: Perform calibrated pipetting, dilution, microscopy, aseptic handling and image-based counting; record provenance, sampling variation and measurement limitations.
Design biological comparisons with controls, replication, randomization, blinding and operational endpoints; distinguish biological from technical replication and causal from observational claims.
Compare scientific value, consent, animal welfare, ecological impact, biosafety and equitable participation and justify a revised study protocol.

practice: Design and execute an approved low-risk microscopy or growth study, including raw records, controls, uncertainty and an ethics revision.

includes: Mendelian and non-Mendelian inheritance, pedigrees, linkage, recombination mapping, quantitative traits and molecular genetic tests.

outcomes.description: Calculate cross and pedigree probabilities, infer linkage and construct recombination maps; distinguish Mendelian, sex-linked, cytoplasmic and quantitative inheritance.
Use complementation, epistasis, deletion, expression and rescue evidence to infer gene function and order pathways, recognizing penetrance and background effects.

practice: Infer a genetic map and pathway from crosses and perturbations, then specify an experiment that distinguishes remaining models.

includes: Sequence formats, dynamic-programming alignment, sequence search, read and variant workflows, phylogenetic likelihood and omics analysis.

outcomes.description: Use reproducible tools for read quality, mapping, variant calling and expression analysis; teach and apply finite-state substitution likelihoods for small phylogenies and assess batch effects, multiple testing and reference bias.
Parse sequence and annotation formats and implement pairwise dynamic-programming alignment with explicit scores, traceback and computational cost; compare alignment and search assumptions.

practice: Implement an aligner and complete a documented variant or expression workflow, validating selected calls and reporting filtering and model sensitivity.

includes: Innate and adaptive immunity, antigen recognition, immune development, host-pathogen dynamics, vaccination, tolerance and immune assays.

outcomes.description: Interpret antibody, flow-cytometric and infection-response data with assay controls; compare pathogen evasion, vaccination, allergy and autoimmunity mechanisms and evidence limits.
Trace innate sensing, antigen presentation, receptor diversification, clonal selection, effector responses, memory and tolerance through explicit cellular interactions.

practice: Infer an immune-response defect from controlled assay data and design a follow-up test that distinguishes cellular from assay explanations.

includes: Bacteria, archaea, microbial eukaryotes and viruses; growth, metabolism, culture, identification, communities and resistance.

outcomes.description: Compare microbial cell and viral life-cycle structures, calculate growth and viable counts and explain metabolic diversity and horizontal gene transfer.
Combine culture, staining, biochemical and sequence evidence for identification; interpret susceptibility and community data and distinguish infection, colonization and mutualism.

practice: Characterize an approved nonpathogenic isolate or supplied isolate records using growth, microscopy and independent identification evidence.

includes: Neural anatomy, membrane and synaptic signals, sensory and motor systems, plasticity, behavior and causal circuit evidence.

outcomes.description: Interpret intracellular and extracellular traces, synaptic responses and circuit diagrams; explain sensory coding, motor organization and mechanisms of plasticity.
Analyze stimulus-response and behavioral experiments using tuning curves and spike summaries and compare lesion, recording and intervention evidence for circuit function.

practice: Analyze neural recordings and a behavioral perturbation study, separating correlation, encoding and causal necessity claims.

includes: Plant tissues, life cycles, meristems, reproduction, photosynthetic physiology, water and nutrient transport, hormones and environmental responses.

outcomes.description: Use locally defined water-potential and gas-exchange models to calculate plant transport and photosynthetic responses and design measurements of nutrient, light or water stress.
Identify plant tissues and organs, trace alternation of generations and explain meristem growth, reproductive development and hormonal coordination.

practice: Measure or analyze stomatal, growth or gas-exchange responses and distinguish physiological regulation from measurement artifacts.

includes: Structured populations, nonlinear ecological dynamics, spatial movement, observation models, state-space inference and predictive validation.

outcomes.description: Construct matrix population, consumer-resource and spatial-patch models, analyze equilibria and stability and implement validated numerical population trajectories.

Separate process from observation error, fit bounded occupancy and state-space models using likelihood and supplied optimization tools and assess identifiability, predictive checks and sampling design.

practice: Fit a dynamic population model to imperfect counts, compare observation assumptions and validate forecasts on withheld seasons or sites.

includes: Low-risk engineered regulatory circuits, metabolic burden, design-build-test-learn cycles, evolutionary stability and containment-aware validation.

outcomes.description: Design a low-risk regulatory or metabolic circuit, predict dynamics and resource burden and choose parts, host context and measurable performance requirements.

Plan and analyze a design-build-test-learn cycle, distinguish model from implementation failure and justify decisions about evolutionary stability, containment, dual-use concerns and deployment boundaries.

practice: Develop a contained low-risk circuit project or complete computational and experimental design dossier with quantitative success criteria, failure analysis and a justified containment decision.

includes: Comparative morphology, major microbial and eukaryotic lineages, organismal life cycles, identification keys, homology and classification.

outcomes.description: Code homologous characters, distinguish convergence from shared ancestry and reconcile morphological and molecular evidence when revising a classification.
Use morphological characters and identification keys to distinguish major protist, fungal, plant and animal groups and compare body plans and life cycles.

practice: Build a documented specimen or image collection, an identification key and a character matrix supporting a proposed classification.

includes: Stoichiometric and regulatory networks, mass-action dynamics, feedback, stochastic reaction models, parameter inference and experimental identifiability.

outcomes.description: Construct stoichiometric matrices and mass-action or enzyme-rate ODEs, analyze conservation, steady states and feedback stability and implement stochastic reaction-event sampling for small networks.
Fit network parameters to time courses and perturbations, calculate sensitivities and assess structural or practical identifiability and design discriminating measurements.

practice: Implement and fit a feedback network in deterministic and reaction-event representations, then choose a perturbation that separates competing mechanisms.

includes: Functional polymer, porous or electronic materials design, multiscale structure-property hypotheses and integrated computational and experimental validation.

outcomes.description: Design complementary structural and performance measurements, distinguish correlation from mechanism and compare reproducibility, degradation, scale and lifecycle constraints in a go-or-no-go decision.
Formulate a testable structure-property hypothesis and select synthesis, processing and molecular-computation strategies for a bounded functional-material target.

practice: Develop and critically test a materials-design proposal using a small computational study and independent characterization and performance evidence.

includes: Molecular partition functions, solution statistics, fluctuations, transition-state theory, master equations and molecular relaxation.

outcomes.description: Construct translational, rotational, vibrational and electronic partition functions and derive equilibrium constants, heat capacities and fluctuation relationships with symmetry and standard-state corrections.
Derive transition-state and activated-rate models, solve finite-state kinetic master equations and relate time correlations and relaxation modes to measurable chemical dynamics.

practice: Predict equilibrium and rate changes from a molecular model and compare transient relaxation with an independently constrained kinetic mechanism.

includes: Multidimensional NMR, tandem mass spectrometry, diffraction structure factors, time-resolved spectroscopy and response-aware inverse fitting.

outcomes.description: Interpret two-dimensional NMR correlations and tandem-MS fragments, derive basic diffraction structure factors and combine structural restraints while accounting for ambiguity and resolution.
Model instrument convolution and kinetic spectral mixtures, implement bounded least-squares response fitting and assess identifiability, uncertainty and alternative structural or dynamical models.

practice: Infer a molecular structure and a relaxation mechanism from complementary supplied datasets, including simulated ambiguities and instrument-response effects.

includes: Analytical equilibria, gravimetry and titrimetry, calibration, detection limits, electroanalysis, absorption spectroscopy and chromatography.

outcomes.description: Explain and operate bounded potentiometric, voltammetric, absorption and chromatographic methods, including instrument response, separation efficiency and method validation.
Design gravimetric, titrimetric and calibrated assays using mass and charge balances; quantify uncertainty, detection limits, recovery and matrix effects.

practice: Develop an assay for a component in a mixture using calibration, spikes, blanks and an independently checked separation.

includes: Protein, carbohydrate, lipid and nucleic-acid chemistry, enzyme kinetics, biochemical energetics and central metabolism.

outcomes.description: Relate biomolecular structure and noncovalent interactions to folding, binding and catalysis; derive the steady-state Michaelis-Menten model and distinguish inhibition mechanisms from rate data.
Trace atoms, reducing equivalents and ATP through central catabolic and anabolic pathways; calculate coupled free-energy and redox balances and explain regulation and compartmentation.

practice: Analyze enzyme-rate data and an isotope-labeling pathway problem, checking kinetic assumptions and matter and energy balances.

includes: Moles, stoichiometry, solutions, atomic structure, periodicity, bonding, molecular geometry and intermolecular forces.

outcomes.description: Use electron configurations, periodic trends, Lewis structures, resonance and three-dimensional molecular geometry to predict bonding, polarity and intermolecular interactions.
Translate formulas and balanced equations into mole, mass, concentration and limiting-reagent calculations with units and significant figures.

practice: Determine an unknown compound's composition from mass data and compare structural models with its measured physical properties.

includes: Operational IR, UV-visible, mass-spectrometric and one-dimensional NMR models and combined molecular structure inference.

outcomes.description: Explain bounded vibration, electronic absorption, ion fragmentation and nuclear-spin resonance models; interpret frequencies, intensities, isotope patterns, chemical shifts, integration and splitting with their limitations.
Infer and rank molecular structures from formulae and complementary IR, mass and NMR data, assign signals and propose discriminating follow-up measurements.

practice: Solve blinded structure-elucidation cases, documenting every assignment, unresolved ambiguity and proposed confirming experiment.

includes: Electronic-structure workflows, finite-basis self-consistency, geometry optimization, force fields, molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo and computational validation.

outcomes.description: Implement a small self-consistent-field calculation from supplied integrals and use established packages for geometry and energy comparisons, testing basis, convergence, spin and method dependence.
Implement pair-potential forces, Verlet dynamics and Metropolis sampling; define temperature and ensemble controls and diagnose energy drift, equilibration, autocorrelation and finite-size effects.

practice: Compare a molecular energy calculation with a small fluid simulation, separating implemented algorithms from package features and quantifying convergence.

includes: Air, water and soil chemistry, speciation, compartment mass balances, transformation kinetics, environmental sampling and chemical-process sustainability.

outcomes.description: Design environmental sampling and chemical assays; calculate speciation and implement spreadsheet compartment updates from stated transfer and reaction rates with mass-balance and step-size checks.
Construct process mass and energy inventories and compare treatment, synthesis and remediation options using exposure pathways, waste, uncertainty and bounded lifecycle evidence.

practice: Analyze a contaminant-release or treatment case with measured chemistry, a time-evolving compartment model and a justified intervention decision.

includes: Main-group trends, symmetry operations, coordination geometry, ligand-field and qualitative orbital models, inorganic mechanisms and crystal structures.

outcomes.description: Compare coordination substitution and redox pathways; calculate unit-cell composition and relate ionic, metallic and network structures to stability and reactivity.
Classify molecular symmetry and coordination geometry, construct qualitative ligand-field and orbital diagrams and predict magnetism, color and main-group bonding trends.

practice: Identify a coordination compound from structural, magnetic and reaction evidence and compare plausible solid-state structures.

includes: Solution preparation, balances and volumetric tools, heating, extraction, filtration, distillation, titration, notebooks and chemical risk assessment.

outcomes.description: Prepare standards and solutions, execute separations and titrations and record observations, recoveries and uncertainties in a reproducible notebook.
Use blanks, replicates and calibration checks to diagnose error; compare hazards, waste, exposure and substitution options and justify a risk-controlled procedure.

practice: Prepare and standardize a solution, separate a mixture and quantify recovery with a notebook, uncertainty budget and approved risk assessment.

includes: Polymerization, molecular-weight distributions, polymer architecture, ceramics, metals, composites, processing and structure-property measurements.

outcomes.description: Compare chain-growth and step-growth polymerization, calculate molecular-weight averages and ideal conversion relationships, and classify crystalline, amorphous and composite structures.
Interpret thermal, mechanical and electrical property measurements; relate processing and degradation to structure and justify material selection using performance and lifecycle criteria.

practice: Compare candidate polymers or composites using synthesis routes, molecular-weight data, stress-strain curves and end-of-life constraints.

includes: Organic nomenclature, conformations, stereochemistry, acidity, curved-arrow mechanisms and major functional-group transformations.

outcomes.description: Translate line, Newman, chair and wedge-dash representations; assign stereochemistry and compare conformational, resonance and acid-base stability.
Construct curved-arrow mechanisms and predict products and selectivity for substitution, elimination, alkene addition, aromatic substitution and carbonyl reactions.

practice: Solve mechanism and stereochemical prediction problems and discriminate plausible mechanisms using rate and product evidence.

includes: Retrosynthesis, carbon-carbon bond formation, enolate chemistry, oxidation and reduction, protecting groups, pericyclic reactions and stereoselectivity.

outcomes.description: Develop retrosynthetic disconnections and forward routes using enolate, organometallic, coupling, redox and pericyclic transformations with compatible conditions.
Predict chemoselectivity, regioselectivity and stereoselectivity; compare routes using yield, step economy, purification feasibility, hazards and evidence needed to verify products.

practice: Design two routes to a stereodefined target and defend the preferred route against likely side reactions and practical constraints.

includes: Born-Oppenheimer separation, molecular orbitals, variational electronic structure, many-electron approximations, molecular symmetry and spectroscopy.

outcomes.description: Apply Born-Oppenheimer and variational approximations, construct molecular orbitals and Slater determinants and derive finite-basis Hartree-Fock equations and correlation limitations.
Use molecular symmetry, transition moments and rotational-vibrational models to calculate spectral patterns and relate potential-energy surfaces to bonding and reaction coordinates.

practice: Construct a small molecular-orbital calculation and predict spectroscopic changes across isotopic substitution or geometry variation.

includes: Gas and solution models, reaction energy, equilibrium, acid-base and solubility systems, redox cells and introductory rate laws.

outcomes.description: Solve acid-base, buffer, solubility and redox-cell problems and infer simple rate laws and Arrhenius parameters from concentration-time and temperature data.
Use ideal-gas and solution models, calorimetric energy balances, equilibrium constants and reaction quotients to calculate composition and direction of change; apply bounded Gibbs-energy relations.

practice: Predict and analyze a titration, electrochemical cell and rate dataset, checking approximations against mass and charge balance.

includes: Organometallic elementary steps, homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, asymmetric synthesis, mechanistic kinetics and process-aware route design.

outcomes.description: Construct catalytic cycles using electron counting, ligand effects and elementary steps; compare homogeneous, surface-site and asymmetric catalytic strategies for a target transformation.
Derive rate and isotope-effect predictions for competing cycles, interpret catalyst resting states and compare routes using turnover, selectivity, deactivation, scale and hazard evidence.

practice: Design a catalytic route and a mechanism-discrimination program using rate laws, labeling and resting-state measurements.

includes: Thermodynamic potentials, chemical potentials, phase and solution equilibria, electrochemical thermodynamics and mechanistic reaction kinetics.

outcomes.description: Derive thermodynamic differential and Maxwell relations, calculate chemical potentials, activities, phase coexistence and electrochemical equilibria and distinguish ideal from nonideal models.
Construct coupled rate equations and derive pre-equilibrium, steady-state and relaxation approximations; discriminate mechanisms using concentration, temperature and transient evidence.

practice: Construct a nonideal phase calculation and fit competing mechanistic rate models, checking balances, approximations and parameter ambiguity.

includes: Randomized, approximation and online algorithms, probabilistic analysis, reductions and representative lower-bound techniques.

outcomes.description: Construct reductions and adversarial or counting lower bounds; distinguish computational, information and model-dependent limitations.
Design randomized, approximation and online algorithms and prove expected, high-probability, approximation-ratio or competitive guarantees using explicitly derived bounds.

practice: Implement a randomized or approximation algorithm and pair empirical results with a complete guarantee and a near-worst-case construction.

includes: State-space search, heuristic search, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, logical knowledge representation and classical planning.

outcomes.description: Represent facts and actions in propositional or first-order logic, implement bounded unification and inference, and construct and validate classical plans.
Implement uninformed and heuristic search, minimax with pruning and constraint propagation; justify completeness, optimality or pruning assumptions.

practice: Build a planner or game agent and compare representations and heuristics using search effort, solution quality and failure cases.

includes: Combinational and sequential logic, finite-state control, instruction sets, datapaths, pipelines, caches and performance measurement.

outcomes.description: Analyze pipeline hazards, cache mappings, locality and memory hierarchy; predict and measure performance using instruction and access traces.
Design arithmetic and sequential circuits, finite-state controllers and a small instruction-set datapath using a logic simulator.

practice: Build a simulated small processor and compare two cache or pipeline configurations on the same program traces.

includes: Geometric transformations, projection, meshes, rasterization, visibility, shading, ray tracing, sampling and keyframe animation.

outcomes.description: Represent two- and three-dimensional scenes with meshes and homogeneous coordinates; implement camera transforms, clipping, rasterization and depth buffering.
Implement local shading and a basic ray tracer, explain sampling and aliasing, and animate rigid objects and spline paths using interpolation.

practice: Render and animate the same scene with rasterization and ray tracing, comparing visibility, illumination approximations and sampling artifacts.

includes: Binary and Boolean representations, integer and floating-point encoding, machine instructions, stacks, heaps and process-level execution.

outcomes.description: Encode integers, characters and floating-point values; evaluate Boolean circuits and explain overflow, precision loss and representation boundaries.
Trace simple instruction sequences, procedure calls and stack or heap memory; relate executable programs to processes, files and permissions.

practice: Inspect a compiled program with a debugger and explain its instruction flow, memory layout and one representation-induced bug.

includes: Symmetric and public-key primitives, number-theoretic constructions, security games, reductions, signatures and key exchange.

outcomes.description: Implement educational modular-arithmetic encryption, signature and key-exchange examples and explain pseudorandomness, encryption modes, hashes and message authentication.
Formulate indistinguishability and unforgeability games, construct attacks and elementary security reductions and compare protocol composition and key-management assumptions.

practice: Break deliberately flawed constructions, prove a bounded reduction and contrast educational implementations with production-library requirements.

includes: Arrays, linked structures, hashing, trees, heaps, graphs, sorting, searching, dynamic programming, greedy methods and asymptotic analysis.

outcomes.description: Implement sorting, graph traversal, shortest paths and representative divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic-programming algorithms.
Prove correctness using invariants and induction and analyze worst-case, amortized and recurrence-based time and space costs.
Implement lists, hash tables, balanced search-tree operations, heaps and graph representations, preserving representation invariants.

practice: Implement a route-planning library with interchangeable graph structures, correctness tests and experimentally checked complexity predictions.

includes: Relational modeling, SQL, relational algebra, normalization, indexes, query plans, transactions and basic nonrelational tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Translate requirements into relational schemas, dependencies and normalized designs; write SQL and relational-algebra queries with constraints and null semantics.
Explain index and join execution, inspect query plans and reason about isolation, serializability, logging and alternative document or key-value models.

practice: Build a transactional application, tune a measured slow query and reproduce then prevent a concurrency anomaly.

includes: Shared-memory and message-passing parallelism, synchronization, distributed failure models, replication, consistency and consensus.

outcomes.description: Implement a replicated log and bounded consensus protocol, specify consistency and failure assumptions and prove safety arguments while testing recovery and liveness limits.
Implement parallel tasks with shared-memory and message-passing models; analyze races, work, span, load balance and communication overhead.

practice: Build a replicated service with fault injection and a parallel batch workload; report correctness evidence, scaling and failure limitations.

includes: Hoare logic, invariants, weakest preconditions, temporal specifications, transition systems and automated verification.

outcomes.description: Specify preconditions and postconditions, derive weakest preconditions and loop invariants and construct Hoare-style proofs tied to an operational semantics.
Express safety and liveness in temporal logic, implement explicit-state model checking and use a supplied SMT solver while analyzing abstraction and state-space limits.

practice: Verify a bounded concurrent protocol and a loop-based program, comparing proofs, model-checker counterexamples and conventional tests.

includes: User research, task analysis, interaction design, accessible prototyping, usability evaluation and participatory ethical judgment.

outcomes.description: Design usability studies, combine qualitative and quantitative evidence and justify interface decisions involving consent, exclusion, manipulation and competing stakeholder needs.
Conduct and analyze bounded interviews or observations, model user tasks and construct paper or interactive prototypes with accessibility criteria.

practice: Iterate a prototype using approved user research or supplied study records and document how evidence changed the design.

includes: Operational semantics, type systems, functional and object-oriented abstractions, parsing, intermediate representations and code generation.

outcomes.description: Implement lexical analysis, parsing, name resolution, type checking, intermediate-code transformation and code generation for a small language.
Define evaluation rules, environments and stores; compare language paradigms and derive typing judgments and elementary type-safety arguments.

practice: Implement an interpreter and compiler for the same small language and test semantic agreement, rejected programs and optimization correctness.

includes: Supervised learning, clustering, dimensionality reduction, gradient training, regularization, validation and model-use judgment.

outcomes.description: Construct leakage-resistant train-validation-test workflows, diagnose overfitting and imbalance, quantify predictive uncertainty and justify deployment or nondeployment using subgroup and harm analyses.
Implement linear and logistic regression with componentwise gradient descent, nearest-neighbor and tree models, k-means and PCA; explain objectives, representations and regularization.

practice: Implement two baseline learners and compare them with a library model on a documented dataset, including leakage checks and a deployment decision.

includes: Packet networks, layered protocols, addressing, routing, reliability, congestion, sockets, DNS and web protocols.

outcomes.description: Trace encapsulation, addressing and routing; calculate latency, throughput and bandwidth-delay effects and implement a small routing simulation.
Implement socket applications and a bounded reliable-transport protocol; inspect packet traces to explain retransmission, congestion, naming and application failures.

practice: Build a client-server service and diagnose injected loss, delay, routing and name-resolution faults from traces.

includes: Processes, threads, scheduling, synchronization, virtual memory, file systems, crash recovery and protection.

outcomes.description: Trace address translation and page replacement, construct a small file-system model and explain protection, persistence and crash-recovery invariants.
Implement scheduling and synchronization exercises using threads, locks and condition variables; diagnose races, deadlock and starvation.

practice: Implement a concurrent service and a simulated virtual-memory or file-system component, including adversarial schedules and crash tests.

includes: Program execution, control flow, collections, functions, recursion, basic objects, files, tests and debugging in one general-purpose language.

outcomes.description: Represent problems with lists, maps and records; use recursion, higher-order functions and simple objects to separate concerns.
Diagnose exceptions and logic errors with traces and a debugger, and write boundary-case and property-based tests.
Write and trace programs using expressions, variables, conditionals, loops, functions and file input/output.

practice: Implement and test a small data-cleaning and reporting application, including malformed input and reproducible output.

includes: Rigid transformations, camera geometry, image filtering and features, robot kinematics, Bayesian localization and collision-free planning.

outcomes.description: Implement image convolution, feature matching, calibrated pinhole projection and triangulation; calculate planar or spatial rigid transforms and manipulator Jacobians.
Implement discrete Bayes and linear-Gaussian Kalman localization, occupancy-grid updates and configuration-space planning; validate uncertainty, collision checks and model assumptions.

practice: Implement a simulated mobile robot that estimates its planar pose from noisy landmarks and plans a collision-free path, reporting localization error and failures.

includes: Threat modeling, memory and web vulnerabilities, authentication, access control, secure protocol use, defensive assessment and incident reasoning.

outcomes.description: Plan an authorized security assessment, validate fixes and analyze incident evidence; justify disclosure, privacy and residual-risk decisions without treating tests as proof of security.

Construct threat models and demonstrate memory, injection, authentication and protocol-use failures in isolated exercises; implement least-privilege and defensive fixes using established cryptographic libraries.

practice: Assess an intentionally vulnerable local application, reproduce selected failures, implement mitigations and deliver a risk-ranked report.

includes: Requirements, modular design, version control, testing, contracts, continuous integration, maintenance and professional obligations.

outcomes.description: Use contracts, unit, integration and property tests to assess quality; justify choices involving reliability, accessibility, privacy, licensing and stakeholder harm.
Elicit requirements, design interfaces and modules, use version control and review, and maintain a tested build and release workflow.

practice: Complete a small team project with requirements traceability, code review, automated tests, a maintenance change and an evidence-based ethics decision.

includes: Statistical learning theory, probabilistic latent-variable models, neural networks, approximate inference and Markov decision learning.

outcomes.description: Derive finite-class and capacity-based generalization bounds using union bounds and concentration inequalities, and relate regularization to estimation and optimization error.
Implement backpropagation, a neural model and an EM or variational latent-variable model; derive their objectives and diagnose optimization and inference failures.
Formulate finite Markov decision processes, derive Bellman equations and implement value iteration and basic reinforcement learning with evaluation separate from exploration data.

practice: Reproduce a bounded learning comparison, including objective derivations, implementation tests, uncertainty and ablations rather than benchmark scores alone.

includes: Finite automata, regular expressions, context-free grammars, pushdown machines, Turing machines, reductions and P versus NP.

outcomes.description: Construct and transform finite automata and regular expressions, build context-free grammars and pushdown recognizers, and prove selected language nonmembership results.
Construct Turing-machine and reduction arguments, prove undecidability examples and establish NP membership and NP-completeness for explicit decision problems.

practice: Give a recognizer construction, a pumping-style impossibility proof and a complete polynomial reduction with both directions justified.

includes: Differential privacy, private optimization, adversarial robustness, distribution shift and evidence-based model auditing.

outcomes.description: Define differential privacy, derive Laplace and Gaussian mechanism conditions and basic composition, and implement clipped noisy-gradient learning with a documented privacy budget.
Construct bounded adversarial and distribution-shift evaluations, distinguish empirical robustness from guarantees and justify an audit decision considering utility, subgroup harms and privacy.

practice: Audit a private predictive model against explicit neighboring-dataset and adversary definitions, including utility costs and negative findings.

includes: Groups, homomorphisms, group actions, rings, ideals, polynomial rings, fields and quotient constructions.

outcomes.description: Construct groups and homomorphisms, compute quotient groups and group actions, and prove isomorphism, orbit-stabilizer and Sylow results with applications.
Calculate with ideals, quotient rings and polynomial factorization; prove basic ring and field results and construct finite field extensions.

practice: Classify small-order examples, construct quotient structures and prove when an explicit quotient is a field.

includes: Affine and projective varieties, coordinate rings, polynomial ideals, morphisms, local rings, tangent spaces and an introduction to affine schemes.

outcomes.description: Relate ideals and varieties using the Nullstellensatz, compute coordinate rings and construct affine and projective morphisms.
Use localization, formal polynomial derivatives, dimension and tangent spaces to detect singularities; interpret prime spectra and regular functions on affine schemes.

practice: Analyze an explicit algebraic curve through its equations, coordinate ring, local singularities and projective completion.

includes: Homotopy, fundamental groups, covering spaces, chain complexes, simplicial and singular homology and basic exact-sequence methods.

outcomes.description: Construct chain complexes, compute homology with boundary matrices and exact sequences, and use invariants to prove nonexistence of maps or deformations.
Compute fundamental groups using van Kampen and analyze covering spaces and lifting properties for explicit spaces.

practice: Compute fundamental groups and homology for cell-built spaces and use them to distinguish spaces with similar pictures.

includes: Limits, differentiation, integration, the fundamental theorem, Taylor approximation and series for one-variable functions.

outcomes.description: Evaluate definite and improper integrals by substitution and integration by parts; use the fundamental theorem, convergence tests and Taylor series with error estimates.
Evaluate limits and derivatives, explain their local meaning, and solve optimization and related-rate problems with assumption checks.

practice: Analyze a motion or growth model using derivatives, integrals and a quantitatively checked local approximation.

includes: Complex differentiation, analytic functions, contour integration, power and Laurent series, residues and conformal maps.

outcomes.description: Calculate contour integrals and residues, classify singularities, evaluate real integrals and construct elementary conformal maps.
Check holomorphicity, derive Cauchy-Riemann relations and prove consequences of Cauchy's theorem and integral formula for analytic functions.

practice: Evaluate an improper real integral by contour deformation and justify all limiting contour contributions.

includes: Parameterized curves and surfaces in Euclidean space, curvature, fundamental forms, geodesics and classical intrinsic geometry.

outcomes.description: Compute arc length, Frenet frames, curvature and torsion for space curves and first and second fundamental forms for parameterized surfaces.
Calculate Gaussian curvature and geodesic equations, distinguish intrinsic from extrinsic properties and verify classical curvature identities on explicit surfaces.

practice: Compare local and global distance and curvature properties of a plane, cylinder and sphere using explicit parameterizations.

includes: Descriptive statistics, elementary probability, sampling and experiments, confidence intervals, tests, regression, resampling and multiplicity without calculus.

outcomes.description: Calculate and interpret standard confidence intervals and tests for means and proportions; use permutation and bootstrap procedures with supplied statistical tools and check assumptions.
Summarize distributions; calculate elementary conditional probabilities and Bayes updates; distinguish random sampling, randomization, confounding and measurement bias.
Fit and diagnose simple and multiple linear regression using supplied tools, distinguish association from causation, and apply familywise and Benjamini-Hochberg multiplicity controls.

practice: Analyze a randomized comparison and an observational dataset, reporting effect sizes, uncertainty, residual diagnostics and limits on causal interpretation.

includes: First-order and linear higher-order ODEs, forcing, Laplace transforms, matrix systems and qualitative stability.

outcomes.description: Solve separable and linear first-order equations, constant-coefficient second-order equations and forced problems using integrating factors, characteristic roots and Laplace transforms.
Solve linear matrix systems using eigenstructure; analyze equilibria and phase portraits, linearize nonlinear systems and state local existence and uniqueness conditions.

practice: Analyze a coupled compartment model and a forced oscillator, comparing exact solutions, transients and phase portraits.

includes: Smooth manifolds, tangent and cotangent bundles, tensors, forms, integration, metrics, connections and curvature.

outcomes.description: Calculate metric connections, geodesics and Riemann and Ricci curvature in coordinates; prove coordinate invariance and compare Riemannian and pseudo-Riemannian examples.
Construct smooth charts and tangent maps, calculate tensor and differential-form transformations and apply exterior differentiation and manifold Stokes' theorem.

practice: Compute a metric's connection and curvature in overlapping charts and verify that an observable geometric quantity agrees.

includes: Counting, recurrences, generating functions, graph structure, trees, matching, flows and elementary extremal arguments.

outcomes.description: Solve counting problems using bijections, inclusion-exclusion, recurrences and formal generating functions, with combinatorial proofs.
Analyze connectivity, trees, planarity, matching and network flow; execute constructive algorithms and prove selected graph theorems.

practice: Construct a matching or flow solution and prove optimality using a combinatorial certificate.

includes: Banach and Hilbert spaces, duality, bounded and compact operators, weak convergence and elementary weak formulations.

outcomes.description: Analyze compact self-adjoint spectra, weak convergence and variational equations; construct elementary Sobolev spaces and prove existence for coercive weak problems.
Establish completeness and duality for standard function spaces and apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness and open-mapping principles with proofs of central cases.

practice: Formulate a one-dimensional boundary-value problem weakly, prove existence and compare its operator spectrum with finite-dimensional approximations.

includes: Field extensions and Galois theory, modules, Noetherian rings, localization and finite-group representations.

outcomes.description: Compute splitting fields and Galois groups and use the Galois correspondence to prove solvability and field-extension results.
Analyze modules, exact sequences, tensor products, Noetherian conditions, prime ideals and localization through constructions and proofs.
Decompose finite-group representations over the complex numbers using invariant subspaces, characters and orthogonality relations.

practice: Compute a Galois correspondence, a localized ring and a character decomposition, explaining the structural information each construction reveals.

includes: Compact forward operators, ill-posedness, spectral and variational regularization, finite-dimensional Bayesian inversion and reconstruction diagnostics.

outcomes.description: Establish nonuniqueness or instability of linear inverse problems using operator spectra and construct discretizations that distinguish resolution from noise amplification.
Implement truncated-SVD and Tikhonov reconstructions, select regularization strength and compare deterministic and finite-dimensional Bayesian uncertainty using held-out or synthetic evidence.

practice: Implement a one- or two-dimensional deblurring inverse problem and report resolution, uncertainty, regularization sensitivity and failure under model mismatch.

includes: Linear systems, vector spaces, linear maps, bases, least squares, eigenvalues and real or complex inner products.

outcomes.description: Compute projections, least-squares solutions, eigenvectors and singular-value decompositions; interpret orthogonal and unitary diagonalization and positive-definite quadratic forms.
Solve linear systems by elimination and represent linear maps through matrices, bases, rank, null spaces and determinants.

practice: Recover parameters from an overdetermined measurement system and compare exact, projected and ill-conditioned solutions.

includes: First-order syntax and semantics, formal proof systems, completeness, compactness, arithmetic encoding and incompleteness.

outcomes.description: Encode syntax arithmetically, relate representability to computation and derive the logical structure and hypotheses of incompleteness and undecidability results.
Construct structures and formal derivations, prove soundness and the main steps of completeness, and use compactness to build or exclude models.

practice: Construct a compactness argument and a detailed incompleteness proof outline that explicitly separates semantic and syntactic claims.

includes: Likelihood, sufficiency, information, asymptotic estimation and testing, decision theory, Bayesian inference and generalized linear models.

outcomes.description: Compare estimators through loss and risk, derive conjugate Bayesian updates and posterior predictions, and evaluate prior sensitivity and frequentist coverage.
Derive estimators, sufficient statistics, Fisher information and likelihood-ratio tests; analyze identifiability, bias, consistency and asymptotic uncertainty, including generalized linear models.

practice: Derive and compare likelihood and Bayesian analyses for a count or binary-response experiment, including an identifiability failure.

includes: Sigma-algebras, measure construction, Lebesgue integration, convergence theorems, product measures and Radon-Nikodym derivatives.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply monotone and dominated convergence, Fatou, Fubini-Tonelli and Radon-Nikodym results with precise hypotheses and counterexamples.
Construct measures from outer measures, distinguish measurable and null sets and define and calculate Lebesgue integrals.

practice: Justify a sequence of limit and integral interchanges and construct examples showing why each major hypothesis matters.

includes: Partial derivatives, gradients, Jacobians, constrained extrema, multiple integrals and vector calculus in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates.

outcomes.description: Evaluate multiple, line and surface integrals with coordinate changes and use Green, divergence and Stokes theorems under stated regularity conditions.
Compute gradients, Jacobians, Hessians and chain rules; use Taylor expansions and Lagrange multipliers to analyze multivariable functions.

practice: Calculate flux through a curved surface in two coordinate systems and verify the result with the divergence theorem.

includes: Divisibility, prime factorization, modular arithmetic, Diophantine equations, quadratic residues and elementary arithmetic functions.

outcomes.description: Solve congruences using the Chinese remainder theorem and modular powers; analyze quadratic residues and prove selected reciprocity consequences.
Use the Euclidean algorithm, unique factorization and arithmetic functions to solve divisibility and linear Diophantine problems with proofs.

practice: Construct complete solution sets for modular systems and compare elementary primality tests with counterexamples.

includes: Floating-point error, conditioning, linear and nonlinear solvers, interpolation, quadrature and initial-value integration.

outcomes.description: Implement interpolation and numerical quadrature, derive elementary error orders and diagnose approximation and roundoff tradeoffs.
Implement Euler and Runge-Kutta ODE solvers; assess convergence, stiffness and step-size sensitivity using exact or refined reference solutions.
Implement pivoted elimination, iterative linear solution, power iteration and bracketed or Newton root finding; distinguish conditioning from stability and test residuals.

practice: Build a tested numerical library and produce convergence studies separating model, discretization and floating-point errors.

includes: Linear and convex optimization, duality, constrained optimality, gradient and Newton methods and discrete optimization formulations.

outcomes.description: Formulate linear, convex and integer programs; derive duals and KKT conditions, prove elementary convexity results and use certificates or counterexamples to assess optimality.
Implement gradient, projected-gradient and Newton methods; execute simplex and branch-and-bound on small examples and assess convergence and sensitivity.

practice: Solve a resource-allocation and a constrained estimation problem, providing primal-dual certificates or documented optimality gaps.

includes: First-order transport, heat, wave and Laplace equations; characteristics, Fourier methods, separation of variables and energy estimates.

outcomes.description: Derive and classify canonical PDEs from conservation laws, solve first-order transport by characteristics and use elementary energy estimates to assess uniqueness and stability.
Construct Fourier and eigenfunction expansions and solve heat, wave and potential problems on intervals, rectangles and radially symmetric domains with explicit boundary conditions.

practice: Solve heat and wave problems with the same initial spatial profile and compare smoothing, propagation and boundary effects.

includes: Discrete and continuous random variables, conditional laws, expectation, joint distributions and elementary probability limits.

outcomes.description: Use joint laws, covariance, conditional expectation, generating functions and convolution; prove elementary inequalities and justify laws of large numbers and central-limit approximations at an introductory level.
Construct probability models, calculate conditional probabilities and transformations, and compute expectations and variances from mass functions and densities.

practice: Derive the distribution and uncertainty of a sum or transformed measurement and compare an exact calculation with a limit approximation.

includes: Propositional and predicate logic, sets, relations, maps, cardinality and standard proof methods.

outcomes.description: Translate statements with quantifiers and use sets, relations, functions, equivalence classes and finite or countable cardinalities precisely.
Construct direct, contrapositive, contradiction and induction proofs; find counterexamples and diagnose invalid arguments.

practice: Write and revise proofs about divisibility, sums, functions and countability, including counterexamples to plausible false claims.

includes: Arithmetic, algebra, functions, elementary Euclidean and coordinate geometry, vectors, trigonometry, complex numbers, units and graphs.

outcomes.description: Solve linear and quadratic equations and manipulate powers, logarithms, rational expressions and function compositions, with domain checks.
Use similarity, the Pythagorean theorem, trigonometry, Cartesian coordinates, vectors and complex arithmetic to solve two- and three-dimensional geometric problems.
Convert units, use dimensional reasoning, interpret slopes and areas graphically, and represent data on linear and logarithmic axes.

practice: Solve a mixed modeling portfolio involving scale drawings, exponential change, vector components and dimensional checks.

includes: Real-number completeness, sequences, metric limits, compactness, differentiation, Riemann integration and convergence of functions.

outcomes.description: Prove fundamental differentiation and Riemann integration results and determine when pointwise or uniform limits commute with continuity, differentiation and integration.
Prove results about completeness, sequences, continuity and compactness using epsilon arguments and metric-space examples.

practice: Develop a proof portfolio featuring a convergence theorem, a counterexample and a repaired theorem with sufficient hypotheses.

includes: Measure-theoretic conditional expectation, martingales, Markov chains, Brownian motion, stochastic integration and diffusion equations.

outcomes.description: Construct conditional expectation and filtrations, prove basic martingale convergence and stopping results and check their hypotheses in examples.
Analyze discrete and continuous-time Markov chains; construct Brownian and Itô models, apply Itô's formula and connect generators to forward and backward diffusion equations.

practice: Derive hitting probabilities and mean passage times using both probabilistic arguments and generator equations.

includes: Topological and metric spaces, bases, products, quotients, continuity, compactness, connectedness and separation.

outcomes.description: Construct topologies from bases and form subspaces, products and quotients; compare metric and topological continuity.
Prove or refute compactness, connectedness and separation properties and use them to distinguish spaces and control continuous maps.

practice: Analyze a quotient-space construction and prove which familiar properties survive the quotient.

includes: Amplifiers, filters, digitization, noise, Fourier signal analysis, lock-in detection, instrument response and advanced measurement inference.

outcomes.description: Automate an advanced optical, electrical or modern-physics measurement; estimate parameters with calibrated response matrices and weighted fits and validate systematic, drift and model-error claims.
Design bounded amplifier and filter chains from taught component models, calculate transfer functions and noise budgets and use discrete Fourier transforms and sampling theory to diagnose signals.

practice: Build or analyze a lock-in, spectroscopy or low-noise sensor experiment with acquisition code, calibration, signal processing and an independently challenged uncertainty budget.

includes: Correlations, Landau-Ginzburg models, critical phenomena, finite-size scaling, Monte Carlo sampling and elementary renormalization.

outcomes.description: Perform real-space coarse graining and elementary renormalization calculations, extract critical exponents and compare finite-size scaling with mean-field and simulation evidence.
Calculate correlation functions and response in Gaussian and mean-field models and implement Metropolis sampling with detailed-balance, equilibration and autocorrelation diagnostics.

practice: Implement a lattice-model Monte Carlo study and infer critical behavior with autocorrelation-aware uncertainty and finite-size checks.

includes: Variational calculus, generalized coordinates, constraints, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics, symmetries and normal modes.

outcomes.description: Derive Euler-Lagrange equations from stationary action, handle holonomic constraints and construct Hamiltonians and canonical equations in generalized coordinates.
Derive conserved quantities from continuous symmetries, compute Poisson brackets and analyze coupled small oscillations through generalized eigenvalue problems.

practice: Derive and analyze a constrained coupled mechanical system in both Lagrangian and Hamiltonian representations.

includes: Astronomical coordinates and observation, photometry, spectra, distances, orbital inference, stellar structure, galaxies and bounded cosmological models.

outcomes.description: Use sky coordinates, calibrated images, magnitudes, parallax, spectra and Doppler shifts to infer distances, temperatures, masses and orbital properties with selection and uncertainty checks.
Apply hydrostatic and energy-balance models to stars and use locally derived Newtonian expansion and redshift-distance relations to analyze galaxies and introductory cosmological evidence.

practice: Infer stellar or exoplanet parameters from calibrated photometric and spectroscopic records and assess degeneracies and observational selection.

includes: Atomic angular momentum and spectra, molecular rotation and vibration, selection rules, line broadening, lasers and coherent light-matter interaction.

outcomes.description: Calculate fine-structure and external-field shifts at introductory perturbative depth, molecular rotational and vibrational spectra and dipole selection rules.
Solve bounded two-level and laser-rate models, distinguish homogeneous and inhomogeneous broadening and infer physical parameters from absorption, fluorescence and resonance measurements.

practice: Assign a spectrum and analyze a resonance or laser dataset, accounting for selection rules, instrumental width and population dynamics.

includes: Crystal and reciprocal lattices, diffraction, phonons, electronic bands, transport, semiconductors, magnetism and superconductivity foundations.

outcomes.description: Construct reciprocal lattices, predict diffraction conditions and calculate one-dimensional phonon and tight-binding dispersions, density of states and elementary band filling.
Calculate bounded transport and semiconductor carrier models and compare magnetic and superconducting mechanisms using heat-capacity, susceptibility and conductivity evidence.

practice: Infer a material model from diffraction and transport data and calculate which further measurement best distinguishes competing explanations.

includes: Continuum kinematics, stress and strain, conservation laws, Newtonian fluids, linear elasticity, dimensional analysis and canonical solutions.

outcomes.description: Construct velocity, strain and stress fields and derive integral and differential mass and momentum balances with Newtonian-fluid and linear-elastic constitutive assumptions.
Solve hydrostatic, Couette, Poiseuille, simple elastic and linear-wave problems; use Reynolds and related dimensionless numbers to justify approximations and identify instability limits.

practice: Derive a pipe-flow or elastic-deformation prediction from balances and compare it with data across the regime where its assumptions fail.

includes: Feedback, transfer functions, frequency response, PID control, state-space models, stability, controllability and observability.

outcomes.description: Derive transfer functions from mechanical equations, analyze poles and frequency response and design PID feedback with explicit stability and performance checks.
Construct state-space models, test controllability and observability and calculate pole-placement feedback and observers for small linear systems.

practice: Design feedback for a motor or oscillator model and compare tracking, disturbance rejection and robustness to parameter error.

includes: Electrostatic and magnetic fields, potential, Gauss and Ampere symmetry methods, capacitance, circuits and Faraday induction.

outcomes.description: Solve resistor and capacitor networks, derive and solve simple RC and RL transients, and calculate induction, field energy and sinusoidal impedance using complex amplitudes.
Calculate electric and magnetic fields and electric potentials by superposition and symmetry-based integral laws for line, plane, spherical and cylindrical configurations.

practice: Predict a circuit transient and an induced voltage, then compare analytic calculations with measured or supplied traces.

includes: Electrostatic and magnetostatic boundary methods, multipoles, material response, Maxwell equations, electromagnetic waves and radiation.

outcomes.description: Solve potential boundary problems using images, separation and Green-function constructions; calculate multipoles and fields in dielectric and magnetic media.
Derive wave and energy equations from Maxwell's equations, calculate reflection and guided modes and obtain retarded-potential and dipole-radiation predictions.

practice: Solve a boundary-value field problem and a radiating-source problem, checking boundary conditions, dimensions and energy conservation.

includes: Calibration, instrument resolution, sampling, uncertainty, elementary sensors and meters, controlled experiments and laboratory decisions.

outcomes.description: Design controlled measurements, propagate independent uncertainties by locally derived sensitivity rules, fit bounded models and justify changes based on residuals, risk and data-integrity obligations.
Calibrate length, time, temperature and low-voltage sensors, use meters and data loggers within taught operating limits and distinguish resolution, bias, drift and random variation.

practice: Complete a calibration and model-testing experiment with a raw-data notebook, uncertainty budget, residual analysis and justified safety choices.

includes: Lorentzian spacetime, stress-energy, Einstein equations, geodesic observables, black holes, gravitational waves and homogeneous cosmology.

outcomes.description: Calculate redshift, orbital and light-deflection observables in Schwarzschild spacetime and analyze linearized waves and FLRW expansion with explicit coordinate and approximation choices.
Construct spacetime and stress-energy tensors, derive geodesic and Einstein equations at standard graduate depth and verify covariance and conservation identities.

practice: Derive an observable relativistic prediction from a metric and compare coordinate-dependent intermediate quantities with invariant results.

includes: Angular-momentum addition, identical particles, second quantization, scattering theory, density operators, open systems and path integrals.

outcomes.description: Add angular momenta, construct symmetrized many-particle states and use creation and annihilation operators for bounded bosonic and fermionic models.
Analyze mixed states, entanglement and elementary master equations; derive time-sliced path integrals for simple systems and recover stationary-action and propagator limits.
Derive scattering amplitudes with partial waves and Born approximations and calculate time-ordered perturbative transition amplitudes with stated validity conditions.

practice: Solve a composite-state, scattering and dissipative two-level problem, comparing state-vector, operator and propagator descriptions.

includes: Calculus-based particle motion, Newtonian dynamics, energy, momentum, rotation and gravitation.

outcomes.description: Derive and solve particle equations in Cartesian and polar coordinates for variable forces, work, momentum and constrained motion using integrals and conservation laws.
Calculate centers of mass, moments of inertia, torque, angular momentum and elementary orbital motion; compare point-particle and rigid-body approximations.

practice: Analyze a rotating mechanical assembly and a central-force orbit, checking coordinate equations against conservation laws.

includes: Special relativity, photons, matter waves, atomic spectra, quantization and elementary quantum probability.

outcomes.description: Calculate photoelectric, Compton, matter-wave and elementary atomic-model predictions; interpret discrete probabilities and continuous probability densities in quantum measurements.
Apply Lorentz transformations and invariant intervals, and calculate relativistic energy, momentum and reaction thresholds in one- and two-particle examples.

practice: Compare classical and modern predictions for benchmark experiments and identify which measured features rule out each classical model.

includes: Bifurcations, nonlinear oscillations, chaos, stochastic differential models, Langevin dynamics, Fokker-Planck equations and relaxation.

outcomes.description: Construct bifurcation diagrams and Poincaré maps, calculate Lyapunov exponents numerically and distinguish chaos, quasiperiodicity and numerical artifacts.

Derive bounded Langevin and Fokker-Planck models from drift and diffusion moments, implement Euler-Maruyama with locally taught Gaussian sampling and assess relaxation, stationary laws and detailed balance.

practice: Study a driven nonlinear oscillator and a noisy bistable system, validating timestep convergence, long-time statistics and transient relaxation.

includes: Nuclear binding and models, decay chains, reactions, scattering, particle symmetries, Standard Model organization and detector evidence.

outcomes.description: Calculate binding-energy, decay-chain, reaction-threshold and cross-section examples and compare liquid-drop, shell and tunneling explanations of nuclear behavior.
Classify particles and interactions by conserved quantum numbers, reconstruct invariant masses from four-momenta and analyze efficiency, background and counting uncertainty in detector data.

practice: Analyze a decay or scattering dataset and reconstruct a candidate resonance while separating physical signal from acceptance and background effects.

includes: Physical idealization, units, measurement, algebraic kinematics, free-body diagrams, energy and momentum.

outcomes.description: Define system boundaries, estimate scales, propagate bounds through simple calculations and compare a dimensional model with plotted measurements.
Solve constant-acceleration, static-force, work-energy and one-dimensional collision problems using vectors, free-body diagrams and conservation laws.

practice: Measure an object's motion using video or a supplied coordinate-time record and test competing force and energy models.

includes: Charged-particle orbits, drifts, Debye screening, plasma frequency, fluid plasma waves and introductory magnetohydrodynamics.

outcomes.description: Calculate charged-particle gyromotion and force drifts, derive Debye screening and plasma frequency and compare characteristic plasma scales and model regimes.
Derive two-fluid and ideal-MHD balances, linearize plane-wave disturbances and calculate elementary electrostatic and Alfvén-wave dispersion and stability conditions.

practice: Calculate confinement and wave scales for a laboratory or space-plasma case and identify where a fluid description ceases to be credible.

includes: Relativistic classical fields, symmetries, scalar and spinor quantization, gauge fields, propagators, Feynman diagrams and introductory renormalization.

outcomes.description: Derive field Euler-Lagrange and Noether relations, construct scalar and Dirac fields using locally developed gamma-matrix algebra and explain gauge redundancy and canonical quantization.
Derive propagators and diagram rules, calculate elementary tree amplitudes and regulated one-loop scalar integrals, and explain counterterms, running parameters and the limits of perturbation theory.

practice: Calculate a simple scattering cross section and a cutoff-regulated scalar correction, checking symmetries, dimensions and regulator dependence.

includes: Interacting lattice models, exact diagonalization, correlation diagnostics, Berry phases and elementary topological bands.

outcomes.description: Construct finite-lattice Hamiltonians in occupation-number bases, implement exact diagonalization using tested eigensolver libraries and calculate spectra, correlations and Berry phases for elementary band models.
Use symmetry, finite-size and parameter sweeps to distinguish phase evidence from numerical artifacts and propose measurable signatures and falsifying comparisons.

practice: Reproduce a finite-lattice phase diagnostic or two-band topological calculation, documenting basis truncation, convergence and limits of the phase claim.

includes: Quantum states and operators, Schrödinger dynamics, one-dimensional potentials, angular momentum, hydrogen, spin and approximation methods.

outcomes.description: Derive angular-momentum commutators and ladder relations, separate the three-dimensional central-potential equation and calculate hydrogen and spin-one-half observables.
Use variational, stationary perturbation and elementary time-dependent perturbation methods to estimate energies and transition probabilities and assess validity conditions.
Normalize states, calculate measurement probabilities and expectations, evolve finite-state systems and solve one-dimensional bound-state, tunneling and scattering problems.

practice: Solve and approximate spectra in one and three dimensions, comparing analytic limits, normalization and observable predictions.

includes: Microcanonical, canonical and grand-canonical ensembles, fluctuations, classical and quantum gases, lattice models and elementary phase transitions.

outcomes.description: Derive ensemble distributions and calculate partition functions, thermodynamic potentials, response functions and fluctuations for discrete and continuous classical systems.
Derive Bose and Fermi occupation laws and calculate ideal quantum-gas observables; analyze elementary spin and mean-field phase-transition models with their limitations.

practice: Calculate thermodynamic and fluctuation predictions for a gas and lattice model, contrasting finite systems and thermodynamic limits.

includes: Temperature, heat, work, ideal gases, first and second laws, entropy, cycles, phase equilibrium and elementary heat transfer.

outcomes.description: Calculate entropy changes and equilibrium criteria, interpret phase diagrams and solve bounded conduction, convection and radiation heat-balance problems with stated constitutive laws.
Calculate heat, work and internal-energy changes along explicit thermodynamic paths and evaluate engines, refrigerators and calorimetric balances.

practice: Compare reversible and irreversible thermal processes and analyze the performance and losses of a simple heat-transfer device.

includes: Harmonic oscillations, damping and resonance, traveling and standing waves, acoustics, ray optics, interference, diffraction and polarization.

outcomes.description: Construct ray diagrams and lens calculations and predict slit, grating and polarization patterns using phase differences and explicitly taught scalar superposition integrals.
Derive harmonic and driven-oscillator responses using sinusoidal trial solutions; calculate wave speed, standing modes, interference, acoustic intensity and Doppler shifts.

practice: Design an optical or acoustic measurement and predict how wavelength, geometry, damping and finite resolution affect the observed pattern.
